§9.2.8 Side-by-Side Mini Tables

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

tables-side-by-side-mini-tables · tables boundaries failure-mode

✅ Normative

Boxes sitting side by side with their own titles and their own schemas MUST be rendered as separate tables — even when their rows line up perfectly. Neighbouring tables MUST NOT be woven together, and a small side table MUST NOT be folded into the middle of another table's body.

Printed:  [Box A]      [Box B]        Woven output (non-conforming):
          | a1 | a2 |  | b1 | b2 |    | a1 | a2 | b1 | b2 |
          | a3 | a4 |  | b3 | b4 |    | a3 | a4 | b3 | b4 |
                                        ↑ rows from unrelated boxes glued together

Weaving is not merely mis-structured. It asserts that a1 and b1 belong to the same record, which the page never said (never invent).

Requirements

  • Each box MUST be rendered as its own table, with its own title and its own header stack.
  • Row alignment MUST NOT be used as a grouping signal. Boxes are top-aligned for looks, so their rows land at the same heights by accident.
  • The title and the schema decide: its own title and its own columns means its own table.
  • A small side table MUST NOT be absorbed into another table's body. A "12pt / 3 Year" side panel is not three extra rows in the claims grid beside it.

Header attribution is per column, not per table

A header owns the columns printed under it, not everything to its right. A title like "Reported Claims" sitting over the claim-count columns does not also claim the year labels beside them. A spanning header MUST span exactly the columns it sits above.

Contrast with the cases that DO merge

The neighbouring cases pull the other way, which is why the title and schema are checked rather than a blanket "boxes are always separate":

  • Column Continuation§9.2.2 — side-by-side blocks that are one series: same schema, headers repeated, key continuing onward
  • Split Tables Sharing a Header§9.2.9 — fragments that must merge: one header, printed once

The discriminator is own title / own schema. If each box declares what it is and how its columns are named, it stands alone.

✅ Sample — a two-sided balance sheet in one frame

Assets down the left, liabilities and equity down the middle, an income statement on the right, all inside one ruled box under two title bands. These are different schemas, not consecutive ranges of a repeated schema. Repeated-schema continuations follow Column Continuation§9.2.2 even inside one enclosing frame. Row n on the left has nothing to do with row n in the middle, and yet this is one table, row n across all blocks — the frame is one grid and is transcribed as the grid it prints. The side-by-side rule above is for boxes with their own frames.
